blocks.en_text: My favorite job ever was as a summer-camp counselor,
blocks.zh_text: 我最喜欢的工作是当夏令营辅导员，

blocks.en_text: where I was basically paid to play games with kids all day.
blocks.zh_text: 基本上就是拿钱整天陪孩子们玩游戏。

blocks.en_text: We played capture the flag, running bases, dodgeball,
blocks.zh_text: 我们玩夺旗、跑垒、躲避球，

blocks.en_text: went swimming in the pool every day.
blocks.zh_text: 每天都去游泳池游泳。

blocks.en_text: And at the end of the day,
blocks.zh_text: 一天下来，

blocks.en_text: I'd be tired, but in a good way.
blocks.zh_text: 我会很累，但是那种舒服的累。

blocks.en_text: Not mentally drained, but physically tired.
blocks.zh_text: 不是精神上的疲惫，而是身体上的累。

blocks.en_text: A satisfied kind of tired
blocks.zh_text: 是一种满足的累，

blocks.en_text: where I'd use my body to complete a hard day's work.
blocks.zh_text: 因为我用身体完成了一天的辛苦工作。

blocks.en_text: Flash forward,
blocks.zh_text: 快进到现在，

blocks.en_text: and my job today looks very different.
blocks.zh_text: 我如今的工作看起来完全不一样了。

blocks.en_text: Even though I'm an exercise scientist,
blocks.zh_text: 虽然我是运动科学家，

blocks.en_text: I don't get to actually do any exercise at work.
blocks.zh_text: 但我在工作中其实根本不做任何运动。

blocks.en_text: Instead, my days consist of staring at a computer screen
blocks.zh_text: 相反，我每天就是盯着电脑屏幕，

blocks.en_text: and sitting in countless meetings.
blocks.zh_text: 还有开不完的会。

blocks.en_text: The transition for me to office work was jarring.
blocks.zh_text: 对我来说，转到办公室工作让我很不适应。

blocks.en_text: I no longer had those same feelings of satisfaction
blocks.zh_text: 我再也找不到以前那种满足感了，

blocks.en_text: at the end of the day's work.
blocks.zh_text: 在一天工作结束的时候。

blocks.en_text: I was still tired, exhausted, actually,
blocks.zh_text: 我还是很累，其实是精疲力竭，

blocks.en_text: but I hadn't used my body at all.
blocks.zh_text: 但我根本没用过我的身体。

blocks.en_text: And this shift that I experienced, I'm not alone in feeling.
blocks.zh_text: 而我经历的这种转变，并不只有我有这种感觉。

blocks.en_text: We are living in the most sedentary era in modern history.
blocks.zh_text: 我们正生活在现代史上最久坐不动的时代。

blocks.en_text: In a single year,
blocks.zh_text: 仅仅一年里，

blocks.en_text: the average adult will now spend a full 187 days,
blocks.zh_text: 普通成年人现在会花整整187天，

blocks.en_text: over half of the year,
blocks.zh_text: 超过半年，

blocks.en_text: sitting or physically idle.
blocks.zh_text: 坐着或身体不动。

blocks.en_text: The bad news is that our bodies weren't designed for this.
blocks.zh_text: 坏消息是，我们的身体并不是为此设计的。

blocks.en_text: I know because I've spent my career as a scientist
blocks.zh_text: 我知道这一点，因为我整个职业生涯都在做科学家，

blocks.en_text: studying the harms of being highly sedentary.
blocks.zh_text: 研究高度久坐的危害。

blocks.en_text: And what scientists have found is that being highly sedentary
blocks.zh_text: 科学家们发现，高度久坐

blocks.en_text: increases your risk of diabetes,
blocks.zh_text: 会增加你患糖尿病的风险，

blocks.en_text: cancer, dementia,
blocks.zh_text: 癌症、痴呆，

blocks.en_text: heart disease and ultimately early death.
blocks.zh_text: 心脏病，最终是过早死亡。

blocks.en_text: Worse, this is true even if you exercise regularly.
blocks.zh_text: 更糟的是，即使你经常锻炼，这一点依然成立。

blocks.en_text: To put it simply,
blocks.zh_text: 简单来说，

blocks.en_text: being highly sedentary, as many of us are,
blocks.zh_text: 像我们很多人一样高度久坐，

blocks.en_text: is toxic.
blocks.zh_text: 是有害的。

blocks.en_text: Let's start with the healthiest people among us
blocks.zh_text: 我们先从我们当中最健康的人说起，

blocks.en_text: to use as an example.
blocks.zh_text: 拿他们当例子。

blocks.en_text: In one study,
blocks.zh_text: 在一项研究中，

blocks.en_text: when highly trained endurance athletes were forced to bed rest,
blocks.zh_text: 当训练有素的耐力运动员被迫卧床休息时，

blocks.en_text: their aerobic fitness levels dropped by about 20 percent
blocks.zh_text: 他们的有氧适能水平下降了大约20%，

blocks.en_text: in just three days.
blocks.zh_text: 仅仅三天时间。

blocks.en_text: What took them months to build
blocks.zh_text: 他们花几个月练出来的东西，

blocks.en_text: was erased in a matter of a long weekend
blocks.zh_text: 在一个长周末里就被抹掉了，

blocks.en_text: with no movement.
blocks.zh_text: 完全不动。

blocks.en_text: This isn’t unique to highly trained endurance athletes.
blocks.zh_text: 这并不只发生在训练有素的耐力运动员身上。

blocks.en_text: If you took a regular, typical, healthy adult
blocks.zh_text: 如果你找一个普通、典型的健康成年人，

blocks.en_text: and forced them to 40 days of bed rest,
blocks.zh_text: 让他们卧床休息40天，

blocks.en_text: their heart would show changes similar to 50 years of aging.
blocks.zh_text: 他们的心脏会出现类似50年衰老的变化。

blocks.en_text: Now, this isn't about missing a workout or two.
blocks.zh_text: 当然，这不是说少锻炼一两次的问题。

blocks.en_text: Exercise only makes up a tiny fraction of your day.
blocks.zh_text: 运动只占你一天中很小的一部分。

blocks.en_text: The toxicity comes from when movement begins to disappear from your life.
blocks.zh_text: 真正的危害在于，活动开始从你的生活中消失。

blocks.en_text: And this begs the question,
blocks.zh_text: 这就引出了一个问题：

blocks.en_text: why isn't exercise alone enough?
blocks.zh_text: 为什么光靠运动还不够？

blocks.en_text: Part of the answer lies in our muscles.
blocks.zh_text: 部分答案就在我们的肌肉里。

blocks.en_text: Our muscles are more than just a machinery that power movement.
blocks.zh_text: 我们的肌肉不只是驱动运动的机器。

blocks.en_text: They're also really important for regulating things like our metabolism.
blocks.zh_text: 它们对调节新陈代谢等功能也非常重要。

blocks.en_text: Let's use blood sugar as an example.
blocks.zh_text: 我们拿血糖来举例。

blocks.en_text: Our muscles are like sponges for blood sugar.
blocks.zh_text: 我们的肌肉就像吸收血糖的海绵。

blocks.en_text: When we regularly use and contract our muscles,
blocks.zh_text: 当我们经常使用并收缩肌肉时，

blocks.en_text: they're like a moist sponge,
blocks.zh_text: 它们就像一块湿润的海绵，

blocks.en_text: soaking up the sugar from the bloodstream.
blocks.zh_text: 把血液中的糖分吸收进来。

blocks.en_text: But when we don’t regularly use and contract our muscles,
blocks.zh_text: 但当我们不经常使用和收缩肌肉时，

blocks.en_text: like a dry and shriveled-up sponge,
blocks.zh_text: 它们就像一块干瘪的海绵，

blocks.en_text: not really good at soaking up anything.
blocks.zh_text: 根本不太能吸收任何东西。

blocks.en_text: Now here's the key.
blocks.zh_text: 关键在于：

blocks.en_text: When we exercise,
blocks.zh_text: 当我们运动时，

blocks.en_text: it rewets the sponge,
blocks.zh_text: 它会把海绵重新浸湿，

blocks.en_text: but eventually that sponge dries out
blocks.zh_text: 但最终这块海绵还是会变干，

blocks.en_text: if you get little to no movement the rest of your day.
blocks.zh_text: 如果你一天剩下的时间里几乎不动的话。

blocks.en_text: So what do we do?
blocks.zh_text: 那我们该怎么办？

blocks.en_text: Well, we need to keep the sponge moist.
blocks.zh_text: 我们需要让海绵保持湿润。

blocks.en_text: Now I’m not going to tell you that we need to move all day.
blocks.zh_text: 我不会告诉你我们需要一整天都在动。

blocks.en_text: Instead, I'm going to suggest that we follow the lead
blocks.zh_text: 相反，我想建议我们效仿

blocks.en_text: of an unlikely place.
blocks.zh_text: 一个意想不到的地方。

blocks.en_text: The tobacco industry.
blocks.zh_text: 烟草行业。

blocks.en_text: In their early days, cigars were their primary product.
blocks.zh_text: 在早期，雪茄是他们的主要产品。

blocks.en_text: But this was the industrial age.
blocks.zh_text: 但那是工业时代。

blocks.en_text: Millions were working in factories,
blocks.zh_text: 数百万人在工厂里工作，

blocks.en_text: and those workers only got short breaks from their lines.
blocks.zh_text: 而那些工人只能从流水线上得到短暂的休息。

blocks.en_text: Certainly not long enough to smoke a cigar.
blocks.zh_text: 肯定不够长到抽完一支雪茄。

blocks.en_text: Thus, the cigarette became the primary focus of the tobacco industry
blocks.zh_text: 于是，香烟成了烟草行业的主要焦点，

blocks.en_text: so that these workers could get their fix in small, short doses,
blocks.zh_text: 这样这些工人就能以小而短的剂量满足烟瘾，

blocks.en_text: a few minutes at a time throughout the day.
blocks.zh_text: 一天中每次几分钟。

blocks.en_text: And if sitting truly is the new smoking,
blocks.zh_text: 如果久坐真的相当于新型吸烟，

blocks.en_text: as the saying goes,
blocks.zh_text: 就像俗话说的那样，

blocks.en_text: then what better way to fight back
blocks.zh_text: 那还有什么更好的反击方式

blocks.en_text: than to use the approach of the tobacco industry?
blocks.zh_text: 比借用烟草行业的做法呢？

blocks.en_text: But instead of smoke breaks,
blocks.zh_text: 但不是抽烟休息，

blocks.en_text: “movement breaks.”
blocks.zh_text: 而是“活动休息”。

blocks.en_text: Short bouts of movement, a few minutes at a time,
blocks.zh_text: 短暂的活动，每次几分钟，

blocks.en_text: sprinkled in throughout the day.
blocks.zh_text: 分散在一天当中。

blocks.en_text: If our muscles need regular use to function optimally,
blocks.zh_text: 如果我们的肌肉需要经常使用才能发挥最佳功能，

blocks.en_text: then outside of any exercise time,
blocks.zh_text: 那么在运动时间之外，

blocks.en_text: we need to be contracting them frequently through movement.
blocks.zh_text: 我们需要通过活动频繁地收缩它们。

blocks.en_text: The question that we asked in my lab is,
blocks.zh_text: 我们在我的实验室里提出的问题是：

blocks.en_text: what’s the least amount of “movement breaks” that we need
blocks.zh_text: 我们最少需要多少次“活动休息”

blocks.en_text: in order to offset the harms of being highly sedentary?
blocks.zh_text: 才能抵消长时间久坐带来的危害？

blocks.en_text: And the answer we found
blocks.zh_text: 我们找到的答案是

blocks.en_text: was a five-minute walk every half hour.
blocks.zh_text: 每半小时走五分钟。

blocks.en_text: This reduced the blood sugar spike after eating by about 60 percent.
blocks.zh_text: 这让餐后血糖的飙升幅度降低了大约60%。

blocks.en_text: That's the size of reduction you would expect to see
blocks.zh_text: 这个降幅，正是你预期会看到的

blocks.en_text: if you put someone on medication
blocks.zh_text: 如果让某人服用药物

blocks.en_text: to manage their blood sugar levels.
blocks.zh_text: 来控制血糖水平时能达到的效果。

blocks.en_text: The cool part is that our participants weren't sprinting or even walking fast.
blocks.zh_text: 最妙的是，我们的参与者并没有冲刺，甚至都没有快走。

blocks.en_text: This was a stroll, they were walking at two miles an hour.
blocks.zh_text: 这只是散步，他们以每小时两英里的速度走着。

blocks.en_text: Now I want to be honest.
blocks.zh_text: 现在我想坦白说。

blocks.en_text: What I’m proposing to you as the answer to our modern sedentary lives
blocks.zh_text: 我向大家提出的、作为应对我们现代久坐生活的答案

blocks.en_text: are five-minute breaks every hour or every half hour.
blocks.zh_text: 就是每小时或每半小时做五分钟的休息活动。

blocks.en_text: The truth is that when I found out that this was the answer,
blocks.zh_text: 说实话，当我发现答案就是这个时，

blocks.en_text: I was disappointed.
blocks.zh_text: 我很失望。

blocks.en_text: My immediate reaction was,
blocks.zh_text: 我的第一反应是，

blocks.en_text: there's no way people are going to do this,
blocks.zh_text: 人们根本不可能这么做，

blocks.en_text: largely because I couldn't realistically do it myself.
blocks.zh_text: 主要因为我自己在现实中就做不到。

blocks.en_text: And so part of me wondered whether this should be the end of the road
blocks.zh_text: 所以我心里有一部分在想，这是不是该到此为止了

blocks.en_text: for my research on movement breaks.
blocks.zh_text: 我关于活动休息的研究。

blocks.en_text: But rather than argue with the data,
blocks.zh_text: 但与其跟数据争辩，

blocks.en_text: I decided to press forward
blocks.zh_text: 我决定继续推进

blocks.en_text: and put it to the test in the real world.
blocks.zh_text: 把它放到现实世界中去检验。

blocks.en_text: With a little help from public radio,
blocks.zh_text: 在公共广播的一点帮助下，

blocks.en_text: we had over 20,000 people try our experiment
blocks.zh_text: 我们让超过两万人尝试了我们的实验

blocks.en_text: to take movement breaks throughout the day,
blocks.zh_text: 在一天中做活动休息，

blocks.en_text: anywhere from every half hour to every two hours for two weeks.
blocks.zh_text: 从每半小时一次到每两小时一次，持续两周。

blocks.en_text: And to my surprise,
blocks.zh_text: 出乎我意料的是，

blocks.en_text: the vast majority of people liked taking movement breaks.
blocks.zh_text: 绝大多数人都喜欢做活动休息。

blocks.en_text: Many wanted to keep going.
blocks.zh_text: 很多人还想继续下去。

blocks.en_text: We had tapped into something that people were craving,
blocks.zh_text: 我们触及到了人们渴望的某种东西，

blocks.en_text: an antidote to our toxic modern lives.
blocks.zh_text: 一剂对抗我们有害现代生活的解药。

blocks.en_text: But what really surprised me
blocks.zh_text: 但真正让我惊讶的是，

blocks.en_text: is that when we asked people what they liked about movement breaks,
blocks.zh_text: 当我们问人们喜欢活动休息的哪一点时，

blocks.en_text: very few touted the physical health benefits.
blocks.zh_text: 很少有人称赞它对身体健康的益处。

blocks.en_text: Instead, what they liked
blocks.zh_text: 相反，他们喜欢的

blocks.en_text: was how the movement breaks made them feel.
blocks.zh_text: 是活动休息带给他们的感受。

blocks.en_text: They loved that they felt energized,
blocks.zh_text: 他们喜欢自己感到精力充沛，

blocks.en_text: that they no longer felt like they were in this brain fog throughout the day,
blocks.zh_text: 喜欢自己不再觉得一整天都处在脑雾之中，

blocks.en_text: that they were able to actually better focus at work.
blocks.zh_text: 喜欢自己在工作中真的能更好地集中注意力。

blocks.en_text: And this really resonated with me and my experiences
blocks.zh_text: 这真的引起了我的共鸣，也让我想起自己的经历

blocks.en_text: as an office worker
blocks.zh_text: 作为一名上班族

blocks.en_text: and how the exhaustion impacted my life.
blocks.zh_text: 以及那种疲惫如何影响了我的生活。

blocks.en_text: I remember when my kids were younger
blocks.zh_text: 我记得孩子们还小的时候，

blocks.en_text: and I'd come home from my office job,
blocks.zh_text: 我下班回到家，

blocks.en_text: I’d open the door
blocks.zh_text: 打开门

blocks.en_text: and they'd greet me with energy and enthusiasm,
blocks.zh_text: 他们充满活力和热情地迎接我，

blocks.en_text: and want me to immediately start playing with them,
blocks.zh_text: 想让我马上开始陪他们玩，

blocks.en_text: and I just didn't have it in me.
blocks.zh_text: 而我就是没有那个力气。

blocks.en_text: I was too drained from the day.
blocks.zh_text: 我被这一天耗得太累了。

blocks.en_text: And that's one of the most striking findings that we see in the lab.
blocks.zh_text: 这是我们在实验室里看到的最惊人的发现之一。

blocks.en_text: Over the course of sitting all day with no movement,
blocks.zh_text: 在整天坐着不动的情况下，

blocks.en_text: people's mood plummets
blocks.zh_text: 人们的情绪会一落千丈，

blocks.en_text: while their fatigue builds and builds.
blocks.zh_text: 而疲劳感则会不断累积、越来越重。

blocks.en_text: And that's because our muscles have a symbiotic relationship with our brains.
blocks.zh_text: 这是因为我们的肌肉和大脑之间有一种共生关系。

blocks.en_text: They're in constant communication.
blocks.zh_text: 它们一直在相互沟通。

blocks.en_text: Our biological need to contract muscle
blocks.zh_text: 我们收缩肌肉的生理需求，

blocks.en_text: is more than just about physical health and metabolism.
blocks.zh_text: 不仅仅关乎身体健康和新陈代谢。

blocks.en_text: It's also foundational to mental and brain health.
blocks.zh_text: 它也是心理和大脑健康的基础。

blocks.en_text: The promising news is that in our real-world experiment,
blocks.zh_text: 好消息是，在我们的真实世界实验中，

blocks.en_text: our participants only averaged four to five movement breaks a day.
blocks.zh_text: 参与者平均每天只做四到五次活动休息。

blocks.en_text: Far below our lab-tested prescription.
blocks.zh_text: 远远低于我们在实验室里测试出的建议量。

blocks.en_text: And yet, they still reduced their feelings of fatigue
blocks.zh_text: 但即便如此，他们的疲劳感仍然减少了

blocks.en_text: by about 25 percent.
And we see this play out in the lab as well.
blocks.zh_text: 我们在实验室里也看到了同样的结果。

blocks.en_text: Something as small as a one-minute walk every hour
blocks.zh_text: 哪怕只是每小时走一分钟这样的小动作，

blocks.en_text: can still largely offset the impact of sitting all day on your mood.
blocks.zh_text: 也能在很大程度上抵消整天坐着对情绪的影响。

blocks.en_text: So even small, short, infrequent movement breaks
blocks.zh_text: 所以，即便是短暂、零散的活动休息，

blocks.en_text: can counter some, not all,
blocks.zh_text: 也能抵消一部分——不是全部，

blocks.en_text: but some of the hidden costs of our sedentary lives.
blocks.zh_text: 但能抵消一部分久坐生活带来的隐性代价。

blocks.en_text: Now one of the biggest concerns I often hear from employers and schools
blocks.zh_text: 我经常从雇主和学校那里听到的最大担忧之一，

blocks.en_text: about movement breaks
blocks.zh_text: 就是关于活动休息，

blocks.en_text: is they worry that it’s disruptive,
blocks.zh_text: 他们担心这会打乱工作，

blocks.en_text: that it'll hurt productivity and performance.
blocks.zh_text: 会损害生产力和表现。

blocks.en_text: But movement doesn't mean you have to stop working.
blocks.zh_text: 但活动并不意味着你必须停下工作。

blocks.en_text: You can have walking meetings, pace around while you're on a call,
blocks.zh_text: 你可以开边走边开的会，打电话时来回踱步，

blocks.en_text: get walking pads,
blocks.zh_text: 买一台走步机，

blocks.en_text: or simply just move around while thinking.
blocks.zh_text: 或者干脆一边思考一边活动身体。

blocks.en_text: But the bigger idea and concept with movement breaks
blocks.zh_text: 但活动休息背后更重要的理念和概念是，

blocks.en_text: is that when you compare brain activity
blocks.zh_text: 当你比较大脑活动时，

blocks.en_text: after movement
blocks.zh_text: 活动之后

blocks.en_text: versus after sitting,
blocks.zh_text: 和坐着之后相比，

blocks.en_text: the differences are so striking.
blocks.zh_text: 差异非常惊人。

blocks.en_text: The brain after movement looks like one
blocks.zh_text: 活动之后的大脑看起来就像是一个

blocks.en_text: certainly far more ready to learn and to work.
blocks.zh_text: 显然更准备好学习和工作的状态。

blocks.en_text: And yet, somewhere along the way,
blocks.zh_text: 然而，在某个过程中，

blocks.en_text: we decided that sitting
blocks.zh_text: 我们认定坐着

blocks.en_text: and staring in front of a computer screen for eight hours straight
blocks.zh_text: 盯着电脑屏幕连续八个小时

blocks.en_text: is the best way to work.
blocks.zh_text: 才是最好的工作方式。

blocks.en_text: And that's where the real challenge lies.
blocks.zh_text: 而真正的挑战就在这里。

blocks.en_text: Productivity culture, convenience culture,
blocks.zh_text: 生产力文化、便利文化

blocks.en_text: and technology are reengineering our lives
blocks.zh_text: 和技术正在重新设计我们的生活，

blocks.en_text: and steadily removing the need for movement.
blocks.zh_text: 并一步步消除我们对活动的需求。

blocks.en_text: We can have groceries delivered,
blocks.zh_text: 我们可以让人把杂货送到家，

blocks.en_text: and robots vacuum our floors without ever getting off the couch.
blocks.zh_text: 机器人会给我们吸地板，我们连沙发都不用下。

blocks.en_text: And the consequences of this reengineering are that we now often see movement --
blocks.zh_text: 而这种重新设计带来的后果是，我们现在常常把活动——

blocks.en_text: As an inconvenience.
blocks.zh_text: 看作一种麻烦。

blocks.en_text: [My laptop is dying. But my charger is all the way upstairs]
blocks.zh_text: [我的笔记本电脑快没电了。但我的充电器在楼上]

blocks.en_text: We see it as an interruption.
blocks.zh_text: 我们把它看作一种打扰。

blocks.en_text: We see it as something to avoid.
blocks.zh_text: 我们把它看作要尽量避免的事情。

blocks.en_text: I saw this play out with my daughter recently
blocks.zh_text: 最近我就在我女儿身上看到了这种情况

blocks.en_text: when I had to drive her to our local library.
blocks.zh_text: 当时我得开车送她去我们当地的图书馆。

blocks.en_text: But when we got there, the parking lot was full,
blocks.zh_text: 可到了那儿，停车场已经满了，

blocks.en_text: so I had to park a little further away in the street,
blocks.zh_text: 所以我只好把车停到稍远一点的街上，

blocks.en_text: and she immediately started complaining that I had parked so far away.
blocks.zh_text: 她立马就开始抱怨我把车停得太远了。

blocks.en_text: Now mind you,
blocks.zh_text: 你听我说，

blocks.en_text: the place I had parked may have added
blocks.zh_text: 我停车的地方可能也就给她多加了

blocks.en_text: an additional 20 seconds of walking to her life.
blocks.zh_text: 20秒的步行时间而已。

blocks.en_text: Not a mile.
blocks.zh_text: 不是一英里。

blocks.en_text: Twenty seconds.
blocks.zh_text: 就20秒。

blocks.en_text: But that moment hit me.
blocks.zh_text: 但那一刻触动了我。

blocks.en_text: Movement had become an inconvenience for my daughter too.
blocks.zh_text: 活动身体对我女儿来说也变成了一件麻烦事。

blocks.en_text: So I gave her a classic dad lecture.
blocks.zh_text: 于是我就给她上了一堂经典的爸爸课。

blocks.en_text: And this was met with a preteen eye roll.
blocks.zh_text: 结果换来的是一个青春期前孩子的翻白眼。

blocks.en_text: But a few days later,
blocks.zh_text: 但几天后，

blocks.en_text: we were leaving a stadium and I was taking the escalator down.
blocks.zh_text: 我们正从体育场出来，我坐扶梯下楼。

blocks.en_text: And as I'm going down,
blocks.zh_text: 就在我往下走的时候，

blocks.en_text: I see something pass by me and I look and it's my daughter,
blocks.zh_text: 我看到有个身影从我身边经过，一看是我女儿，

blocks.en_text: taking the regular set of stairs --
blocks.zh_text: 她走的是普通的楼梯——

blocks.en_text: happily taking the regular set of stairs --
blocks.zh_text: 开开心心地走普通楼梯——

blocks.en_text: smiling at me as she goes by.
blocks.zh_text: 经过时还冲我笑。

blocks.en_text: It was a small victory.
blocks.zh_text: 这是一次小小的胜利。

blocks.en_text: And if my eye rolling preteen can make this shift on occasion,
blocks.zh_text: 如果我这个爱翻白眼的青春期前孩子偶尔都能做出这样的改变，

blocks.en_text: then I have hope for the rest of us.
blocks.zh_text: 那我对我们其他人也抱有希望。

blocks.en_text: Because movement breaks are ultimately about something bigger.
blocks.zh_text: 因为活动休息归根结底关乎一件更大的事。

blocks.en_text: They're about seeing those small moments in your day
blocks.zh_text: 它关乎去发现你一天中那些小小的时刻，

blocks.en_text: when you have the opportunity to move,
blocks.zh_text: 当你有机会活动身体的时候，

blocks.en_text: to see them not as inconveniences,
blocks.zh_text: 不把它们看作麻烦事，

blocks.en_text: but as a way to reconnect our bodies and our brains
blocks.zh_text: 而是看作让我们的身体和大脑重新连接的方式，

blocks.en_text: so we're not living some tired, drained version of ourselves.
blocks.zh_text: 这样我们就不会活成疲惫不堪、精力耗尽的自己。

blocks.en_text: Thank you.
blocks.zh_text: 谢谢。

blocks.en_text: (Cheers and applause)
blocks.zh_text: （欢呼和掌声）
